observation.visible_scene: A round cooking pan with a dark red/maroon interior and a metallic rim sits filled with a vigorously bubbling clear liquid. Two smartphones lie submerged side by side in the liquid: on the left, a dark phone whose screen is ON, displaying a bright white rectangular message/notification box above a bottom dock of four app icons (a green phone icon at far left); on the right, a white/silver phone lying at a diagonal with its screen OFF (black), its round home button visible at the lower end. A metal pan handle loop appears intermittently at the left edge of the frame. White foam and clinging bubbles outline the edges of the right phone throughout.
visible_changes: Continuous, energetic boiling: small bubbles form across the pan floor, rise, and pop, with the pattern of bubbles and surface foam changing from frame to frame while the overall boil intensity stays roughly constant.
The white foam and bubble clusters around the right phone's edges grow, thin, and shift position as bubbles attach and burst.

Both phones remain in essentially the same relative arrangement (left phone vertical, right phone angled to its upper right); they only jiggle/rotate slightly in place, consistent with being stirred by the rising bubbles rather than translating.
The dark screen of the right phone shows moving bright reflections and bubble patches that drift across its surface.
The left phone's screen stays lit with the same white notification box and dock icons for the whole excerpt, with only minor brightness/flicker changes.
Framing of the pan shifts slightly (the rim, the left handle, and the top edge move relative to the frame borders), indicating small handheld camera movement/tilt rather than the pan itself moving.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the liquid to boil (no heat source or stove is visible) and whether the phones were placed before or during the boil.
Whether the phones are being damaged or survive the submersion; no outcome is shown.
The exact text on the left phone's screen and the identity of the liquid.
What happens before the first frame or after the last frame.
uncertain_details: The small positional shifts of the phones could be partly water-driven jitter and partly camera motion; the two are hard to separate cleanly.
The left screen's content may be static or may be updating in ways too blurry to confirm.
The white patches on the right phone are ambiguous between bubbles/foam on top of the screen and reflections within the liquid.
